transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2029-01-23
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE); Ravi Menon (Redwood SE); Lena Ortiz (Zenara Head of Partnerships); Tobias Kline (Zenara Solutions Architect); Maya Singh (Zenara Channel Ops)

Auto-summary (auto):
- Intro to partnership model (reseller + technical integration).
- High-level feasibility: private/VPC and dedicated capacity look promising; need deeper technical dive on peering and KV cache behavior.
- Action items: deck, pilot pricing, network diagram, technical deep dive.

Topics (auto):
1) Partner model & commercials
2) Deployment patterns: hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC
3) Performance: latency, batching, KV cache, quantization
4) Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, audit logs
5) Next steps: pilot & technical deep dive

-- Transcript --
00:00 Sofia Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick us off, i'm sofia from redwood, and with me is ravi, our solutions engineer.
00:14 Lena Ortiz: thanks sofia, lena here — excited to learn more. quick note we got a bunch on the page so want to be pragmatic.
00:22 Ravi Menon: hey all — ravi, SE. i focus on deployment patterns and perf tuning. we'll try and map how redwood looks as a reseller offering in zenara's portfolio.
00:33 Tobias Kline: Tobias here. i'm the solutions architect — i'll be the technical point for zenara. we run a reseller channel for infra and want to understand runbooks and network/peering.
00:45 Maya Singh: Maya — i handle channel ops, onboarding, and contracting questions. can we cover margins and pilot terms?
00:55 Sofia Patel: absolutely. high level: redwood does hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and private vpc/on-prem. partner model we often do is reseller with co-sell & revenue share, plus a technical integration so you can offer a one-click onramp for customers.
01:10 Lena Ortiz: good. what does one-click mean operationally? like does zenara provision redwood dedicated on behalf of customers?
01:20 Sofia Patel: typically yes — zenara can provision dedicated pools in your account or we can host and white-label the experience. There are two common patterns: 1) Zenara-managed dedicated (we ship an infra bundle that runs in your cloud/region) or 2) Redwood-hosted with reseller billing. Pros/cons depend on data residency and SSO.
01:36 Tobias Kline: for a lot of our customers data residency's a checkbox. we need private vpc peering, KMS key control, and audit logs. does redwood support kms/hsm integrations per-tenant?
01:48 Ravi Menon: yes — for private we surface KMS integration and you can bring your own key. audit logs, RBAC and SAML SSO are available. small caveat: for on-prem air-gapped installs you manage keys locally.
02:02 Lena Ortiz: and SLA's on dedicated? our customers ask for 99.9 and latency guarantees.
02:08 Sofia Patel: with dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime and configured latency targets; depends on commit level and region. we can size GPU pools for throughput to meet P95 goals.
02:20 Tobias Kline: ok. i'd like to dig into perf — what's the expected P95 for a 512-token generation on a quantized Llama-like model running on a T4-ish equivalent? i'm giving example numbers.
02:33 Ravi Menon: rough ballpark — on modern A100/vb100 equivalents we hit low 100-200ms for 512 tokens with optimized kernels and kv caching. on T4-class hardware it'll be higher; quantization and batching change the story. we do kernel selection based on sequence length distribution and model arch.
02:50 Tobias Kline: kernel selection, right. how deterministic is that? i worry about variance if we route between different instance types.
02:59 Ravi Menon: good question — we have smart routing policies. you can pin traffic to variants or allow auto-fallback. variability comes from heterogenous pools; we recommend consistent instance types for strict SLOs or a pinned model variant with canary fallback.
03:14 Maya Singh: can you speak to caching — we've heard of KV cache but our infra team calls it the "kay vee cache" and they get confused. how does prefix caching work with multi-tenant customers?
03:26 Ravi Menon: yeah the terms vary. prefix/KV cache stores decoder past keys so repeated prefixes are cheap. in multi-tenant setups cache is scoped to customer/token since we never cross-tenant data. caching reduces token cost but can complicate cold-starts for new sessions.
03:40 Lena Ortiz: and that affects billing? if customers reuse prompts, they'd cost less?
03:45 Sofia Patel: exactly. we expose token-level billing and cache delta reporting in the console so partners can see unit economics. that's often a sell point for cost-sensitive customers.
03:58 Tobias Kline: network — peering and egress. many of our customers care about egress charges and hop counts. how does redwood handle peering and sizing for dedicated pools?
04:10 Ravi Menon: for private/vpc we do customer-managed peering. We provide an AMI/container config and a small control plane to orchestrate. Egress is typically billed by cloud provider; we can architect inside your VNets to minimize cross-zone egress.
04:25 Lena Ortiz: any special firewall/NAT or proxy requirements? some of our regulated customers require explicit allow lists.
04:31 Ravi Menon: yes we provide explicit outbound endpoints and IP ranges for allow-listing. for air-gapped we'll support an offline package.
04:40 Maya Singh: business model — do you prefer reseller margin up front or referral? we typically do 20-30% margin on infra resale.
04:48 Sofia Patel: both are fine. typical is reseller margin on reserved capacity + revenue share on hosted. we also have pilot credits to reduce friction. we can be flexible depending on minimum commitments.
04:59 Lena Ortiz: competitive positioning — our team sometimes hears Pylon Compute and Aurora as alternatives. why should we put redwood in our catalog?
05:08 Sofia Patel: our differentiator is production-first: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, observability down to token level, and a set of cost/perf levers — batching, caching, and quantization suggestions that are automated.
05:20 Tobias Kline: i want to see real benchmarks with your kernel choices; we've had cases where quantization introduced hallucination regressions. do you run evals tied to prompt sets?
05:31 Ravi Menon: yes — we integrate evals into rollouts. we can tie quality regressions to prompt sets and alert. quantization is model-dependent; we provide recommended quant profiles and regression tests.
05:44 Lena Ortiz: what's the onboarding timeline for a pilot? our customers want a three-week POC usually.
05:50 Sofia Patel: typical pilot: week 0 setup & network + creds, week 1 sizing & simple benchmarks, week 2 integration test and smoke, week 3 handoff. we can compress or extend.
06:04 Tobias Kline: for pilots we'd want to run a representative workload with our LLM quotas: 200 concurrent sessions, peak 250 req/s, median payload 256 tokens. can you simulate that?
06:17 Ravi Menon: yes we can run scale tests. we'll need your expected distribution for sequence lengths and concurrency. we can pre-configure batching windows and autoscale thresholds to hit throughput targets.
06:29 Maya Singh: security paperwork — do you have a partner security questionnaire and SOC2 report we can share?
06:35 Sofia Patel: yes — we'll share SOC2 Type II, and a partner security pack with KMS/HSM notes. also can provide a minimal SSP for quick review.
06:45 Lena Ortiz: great. tricky bit is customers who want reseller to be able to provision dedicated in their own clouds and manage keys. will redwood accept a model where zenara provisions but redwood supports upgrades/patches?
06:57 Ravi Menon: we support that split-responsibility model. operationally we provide a control plane agent and a managed upgrade path — zenara runs the infra but we ship the runtime images and assist on upgrades.
07:12 Tobias Kline: let's talk observability: what traces, token-level metrics, and per-request logs do you share with partners?
07:21 Ravi Menon: console exposes per-route and per-token cost, latency histograms, traces (linkable with Jaeger-style IDs), and optional raw request logs if the customer opts in. audit logs for config changes are always available.
07:36 Lena Ortiz: about pricing: pilot vs committed — do you have a reseller price list or is it bespoke?
07:42 Sofia Patel: reseller price list exists but we typically do a bespoke quote for reserved pools. we'll share a starter price sheet and recommend commit tiers.
07:52 Tobias Kline: edge case: some of our smallest customers want an embedded inference offering — can you support a mini-inference instance on CPU or low-GPU in a reseller-managed fashion?
08:03 Ravi Menon: we can support smaller instances but the cost/perf needs to be considered. for low-cost embedding-only use cases, CPU-based or small-accelerator configs are possible. we can propose a quantized embedding pipeline optimized for that.
08:20 Maya Singh: partner enablement: what assets do you provide — training, sales decks, integration docs?
08:26 Sofia Patel: partner portal with onboarding docs, integration samples, a co-branded deck, and periodic enablement webinars. we also offer an SE sandbox workspace for partner engineers.
08:38 Lena Ortiz: i'd like to flag some integration concerns from our infra team: TLS mutual auth needs to be supported for inter-service communication, and we prefer s2s tokens rotated daily.
08:50 Ravi Menon: we support mTLS for private links, and token rotation via our recommended secrets manager patterns. we'll include recommended rotation scripts.
09:02 Tobias Kline: latency targets again — can you give a concrete example of how you'd route requests to satisfy a <200ms P95 for our european customers?
09:12 Ravi Menon: we'd recommend regional dedicated pools in eu-west, pinned model variant, tight batching settings (small batching window to avoid added latency), and local KV cache warmers. also autoscale thresholds tuned to pre-warm capacity at traffic spikes.
09:30 Lena Ortiz: are there any gotchas around model fallbacks if a variant is unavailable? some customers fear silent model downgrades.
09:38 Sofia Patel: we have explicit fallback policies. we never silently swap to an incompatible model; fallbacks are constrained to compatible model variants and annotated in responses. rollouts use canaries and you can enable automatic fallback if desired.
09:52 Tobias Kline: about telemetry — would zenara get per-customer token and cost data so we can bill downstream customers?
09:58 Sofia Patel: yes, partners can get billing exports and token-level usage reports so you can split charges. we have APIs for usage export which many partners hook into their billing systems.
10:12 Maya Singh: procurement — do you require a master reseller agreement or can we start with an MSA-lite for pilots?
10:19 Sofia Patel: we can do an MSA-lite for pilots then convert to full reseller MSA for production. legal can tailor terms on data residency and indemnities.
10:30 Lena Ortiz: cool. at this point i'd like to share a quick high-level of zenara's go-to-market: we target mid-market SaaS and regulated fintechs, many in eu, with emphasis on embedded AI features.
10:44 Tobias Kline: and from a tech perspective our typical customer profiles: 100-1k RPS peaks, mostly want private deployments or zonal dedicated instances.
10:54 Ravi Menon: makes sense; that profile maps to dedicated pools with conservative autoscale.
11:02 Sofia Patel: ok, should we note immediate blockers? network diagram and sequence distribution from your end; we'll produce a pilot plan and starter pricing.
11:12 Lena Ortiz: yes, and security questionnaire.
11:18 Tobias Kline: i'll run the throughput numbers and share a network topology by next week.
11:24 Maya Singh: i'd also like a templated reseller agreement to review.
11:30 Sofia Patel: we'll send a partner starter bundle after this call.
11:36 Ravi Menon: for the technical deep dive we'll want to go into model-specific kernel choices, quant profiles, and show a live bench run — is next tuesday okay?
11:46 Tobias Kline: tuesday works. prefer morning CET.
11:50 Sofia Patel: noted.
11:52 Lena Ortiz: any last questions?
11:55 Maya Singh: margin discussions — can we set up a follow-up with your commercial team?
11:59 Sofia Patel: yes i'll loop in commercial.
12:02 Sofia Patel: recap quick: we'll send partner deck & pricing, security pack (SOC2 + SSP), and schedule a technical deep dive next tuesday. zenara will send topology, throughput distribution, and procurement lead.
12:16 Lena Ortiz: perfect. thanks everyone.
12:20 Sofia Patel: thank you, talk soon.

End of transcript.
